title: Is the Hivemind Effect Stronger in Code Than in Prose? Safety in Shared Code Patterns

original_idea.body:
# Is the Hivemind Effect Stronger in Code Than in Prose? Safety in Shared Code Patterns

**Problem:** Correlated Errors noted LLM-written code has lower variance. When models generate security-relevant code, do they converge on the SAME insecure patterns?

**Direction:** Use code-generation prompts admitting secure and insecure solutions. Sample from several open code models, run a static analyzer for known vulnerability classes, and measure whether the SAME vulnerability appears across models above chance.

**Why it matters:** Shared insecure code defaults mean one class of bug ships everywhere - a supply-chain threat.

**Relevant context:** Correlated Errors in LLMs (arXiv:2506.07962); homogeneity framing.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible supply-chain risk (shared insecure defaults) but the catastrophic-AI-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Code generation plus off-the-shelf static analysis; accessible with public benchmark.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused: measure shared vulnerability appearance across models; clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public code models and free analyzers; correlated-insecurity angle labs underweight.

novelty.reasoning: Lower code variance noted; shared-insecure-pattern cross-model measurement partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Code-variance observation exists; cross-model shared-vulnerability mapping is an open slice.
